A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaLFL and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite the title change, reformatting, and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original regression and classification experiments, including test performance, learning curves, ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds learning-rate sensitivity results, held-out generalization curves, and MetaLR runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The neural loss representation, smooth leaky ReLU, offline initialization, and one-step online meta-updates remain unchanged. Corrected pseudocode loop bounds agree with step counts already stated in v2 and do not establish a different training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Communities and Crime, Diabetes, California Housing, MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN for the same regression and classification tasks. The added MNIST analyses change settings and measurements within existing coverage.

E2.justification: MetaLR was already evaluated in v2 Appendix D.1, so its appearance in v3 Table 1 largely consolidates existing comparisons. However, v3 newly includes MetaLR in the learning-curve comparison in Figure 3 and the runtime comparison in Table 2.

E3.justification: New Appendix D.3 varies the online meta-learning rate from 10^-1 to 10^-6 on MNIST/LeNet-5. New Appendix D.5 introduces separate training, validation, evaluation, and testing subsets, reserving evaluation data for monitoring generalization. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds targeted MNIST/LeNet-5 analyses of meta-learning-rate sensitivity and generalization during training in Appendices D.3 and D.5. Existing inner-step, loss-representation, activation, and training-versus-validation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V3 adds shaded variability bands around the mean learning curves in Figures 3 and 7, whereas v2 shows mean curves alone. The bands' statistical definition is unspecified. Both versions retain ten independent runs, matched initializations across seeds, and mean ± standard deviation reporting in tables.

E6.justification: MetaLR's CIFAR-10/AllCNN-C test error changes from 0.0656 ± 0.0017 in v2 Table 3 to 0.0672 ± 0.0068 in v3 Table 1; the reason is not stated. V3 adds MetaLR learning curves and runtimes plus MNIST sensitivity and generalization results. Other matched performance-table entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–25 retain the bilevel formulation, gradient decompositions, neural loss definition, and smooth leaky ReLU derivation. No substantive mathematical assumption, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal claims about online adaptive loss learning and performance remain substantively unchanged. The conclusion adds adaptive label-smoothing regularization to the claimed emergent behaviors, alongside learning-rate scheduling and early stopping.

C2.justification: V3 adds the adaptive label-smoothing interpretation, interpretations of the new sensitivity and generalization analyses, and a proposal for less frequent meta-updates to reduce cost. It also omits v2 Section 5's explicit caveat about unstable initialization on CIFAR-100.

D1.justification: Section 4 replaces the redacted code-repository placeholder with a specific GitHub address. Appendix C newly explains validation-based baseline hyperparameter selection. Initialization guidance corrects Sinner < 1 to Sinner > 1 for the optional implicit-differentiation discussion; existing numerical training settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations including Barron (2019), Raymond (2024), Adam, and the regression dataset sources. It connects the new label-smoothing interpretation to prior loss-learning research. The central online-versus-offline positioning remains, while publication and bibliographic updates do not introduce different cited works.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled Meta-Learning Adaptive Loss Functions, with rewritten contribution and results paragraphs and localized subsection changes. MetaLR and runtime discussion become more prominent in the main text, and appendices are reorganized. Much of the introduction, method, and related-work prose remains.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a single-column layout, consolidates result tables, relocates the runtime table, expands Figures 1 and 4, and redraws learning curves with logarithmic axes, bands, and revised legends. It adds Table 6 and Figure 8 while retaining the extended appendix plots. Figure 7's legend is corrected, but Figure 3 introduces several metric-label errors.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens assessment with targeted sensitivity and independent held-out generalization analyses, adds variability displays and MetaLR runtime comparisons, and provides a concrete code address. These improve evidential support and reproducibility information without substantially changing the central findings. Benefits are partly offset by undefined uncertainty bands and incorrect metric labels in Figure 3, supporting a limited overall improvement.
